pages.text: The $(thing)Book Binder$() is altar, desk, and patient accomplice. It binds descriptive books and linking books; the Wayfarer's Primer has its own crafting recipe. In the Binder you may lay loose symbols or a filled notebook in order before the first dangerous reading.
Do not be distracted by the dark panels. The blue field is the name-place. Whatever you write there becomes the Age's first true name when the descriptive book is opened.

The binder is fussy in the way old magic is fussy. Spaces are bound into underscores, unclean marks are replaced, and a repeated name gains a number. Thus one door does not steal the threshold of another.

The $(thing)Writing Desk$() is the quieter place for proper authorship. Set a descriptive book to the left and a notebook to the right, and the desk will copy the notebook's ordered leaves into the book without disturbing the notebook itself. The same desk also lets you rename a linked Age in calm, visible script.

The $(thing)Editing Table$() is stranger work. Lay an unlinked descriptive book in its cradle and surround it with up to 16 of each chosen material. Diamonds tune turbulence, gold sets sea level, iron adjusts cave density, copper changes biome size, and coal changes vertical range.

One spawner writes No Mobs, one sponge removes aquifers, one ender pearl forces a Cave World, and one golden shovel forces Superflat. Only an unlinked book accepts terrain tuning. The ingredients are consumed when the impression is applied and stored until the book first creates its Age.

A linked descriptive book invites sterner work: with a $(item)Curse Cleansing$() page, one ink vial, four lapis, and one amethyst shard, the table removes the strongest active curse and lowers instability by that curse's relief value.

The $(thing)Printing Table$() is for finished work. Set a notebook with an empty page and the press will publish the chosen leaf as a loose symbol page. Set a descriptive book or linking book with leather and it will make a careful duplicate, preserving the written name and all bound marks.

The table takes its due only when you lift the result away. Until then it is a proof and not a commitment. If a notebook holds many leaves, use the arrows to choose which page shall be drawn forth into the world.

Take care with copied descriptive books. They are not new Ages, but additional copies of the same binding lineage. So long as one tracked copy survives, no loss is recorded. If the last copy despawns, burns, falls into the void, or is otherwise destroyed, its Age suffers $(thing)200 instability$().
